_doc: Dart & Flutter MCP server (`dart mcp-server`). JSON has no comments, so these _-prefixed keys document the setup and are ignored by the loader. Functional config = mcpServers.dart.args. GOTCHA: `dart mcp-server --help` claims all features are enabled by default, but that is FALSE for 5 tools — run_tests, get_app_logs, get_active_location, list_running_apps, list_devices are enabledByDefault=false and must be turned on with `--enable`; `--disable` alone leaves them OFF (verified 2026-06-19 by probing tools/list over stdio: --disable-only advertises 9 tools, adding --enable surfaces all 5). So args carry BOTH `--disable <deny-list>` (remove default-on tools) and `--enable <list>` (add the default-off ones). analyze_files/lsp aren't in either arg — they're root-gated and register only once the client supplies a workspace root. The _enabled / _disabled keys below mirror the resulting set.
_enabled: lsp                      — semantic code queries (definitions, references, hover, symbols)
get_runtime_errors       — runtime errors from the running app
get_app_logs             — the running app's log output
hot_reload               — inject changed code into the running app (keeps state)
hot_restart              — restart the running app (loses in-memory state)
list_running_apps        — Dart/Flutter apps connected via DTD (not OS processes)
dtd                      — Dart Tooling Daemon connection (backs the runtime tools)
roots                    — workspace package discovery (which pubspec packages are in scope)
read_package_uris        — resolve package: URIs to on-disk files
rip_grep_packages        — ripgrep across package sources (incl. dependencies)
_disabled: launch_app                     — starts an app instance (you own the lifecycle)
flutter_driver_command         — drives the UI (taps/typing → can mutate your data)
flutter_driver_user_journey_test — drives the UI (can mutate your data)
